source.title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining
source.authors: Ishaan Shah; Anthony M. Polloreno; Karl Stratos; Philip Monk; Adarsh Chaluvaraju; Andrew Hojel; Andrew Ma; Anil Thomas; A. Tanwer; Darsh J. Shah; Khoi Nguyen; Kurt Smith; Michael Callahan; Michael Pust; Mohit Parmar; Peter Rushton; Platon Mazarakis; Ritvik Kapila; Saurabh Srivastava; Somanshu Singla; T. Romanski; Yash Vanjani; A. Vaswani

record.tranche_reason: The study compares Muon and AdamW on pretraining loss and compute-time efficiency, but does not measure held-out test error or the training–test generalization gap required by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The authors use training loss on new batches as a proxy for generalization error, but report no separate held-out evaluation or training–test gap. The batch-size and optimizer results therefore do not test the mapped versions.
record.test_reason: The batch-size experiments bear on V5 in streaming language-model pretraining. Runs use fixed token budgets across batch sizes, and loss is measured on new batches before those data are learned. Section 2.2, footnote 3 therefore supplies a generalization-error proxy despite the absence of a separate held-out dataset. Appendix D.1 reports increased token consumption beyond a batch-size threshold, indicating worse fresh-data loss at a fixed token budget. The Muon–AdamW comparison does not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the optimizer-efficiency conclusion. It omits the authors' second main conclusion: Muon supports muP hyperparameter transfer up to 3.7B parameters, and their telescoping sweep controls transfer errors while reducing tuning cost.
record.recipe_differences: Language-model pretraining with Muon versus AdamW; the study measures tokens and time to training-loss targets, not the claim versions’ held-out generalization outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer advantage is examined across batch sizes, model sizes, data distributions, and architecture ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon requires fewer tokens than AdamW to reach the same fresh-batch loss, with its relative advantage persisting or growing at large batch sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon improves data efficiency and the compute-time frontier relative to AdamW in the tested language-model pretraining setups.

record.problems: No separate held-out dataset is reported for the optimizer and batch-size comparisons; training loss on new batches is used as a proxy for generalization error. Numerical results for the token-ratio curves are presented mainly in figures.

untested.parts: Generalization after width exceeds that needed for zero training error; the width-scaling experiments do not establish interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of locality.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, including tuning-dependent differences.
Repeated-data fixed-epoch training, image classification, and controlled tests of longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization as remedies.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Within-optimizer batch-size results: both optimizers have a token-optimal batch size of 3.5M at DCLM loss 3.25, after which token requirements increase, more slowly for Muon. Add separate rows for AdamW and Muon, recording the fresh-batch evaluation protocol and fixed 25B-token run budget.
missing.locator: Section 2.2 and footnote 3; Appendix D.1; Figure 10, bottom panels

missing.what: Batch-size dependence of tokens needed for fixed fresh-batch losses across architecture, dataset, and model-size ablations. These curves provide relevant scope information beyond the optimizer-ratio row.

record.verdict_notes: A separate held-out dataset or training–test gap is not required by V5. Here the fresh-batch protocol supplies relevant unseen-data loss evidence. The fixed-token streaming setting differs from repeated-data fixed epochs, so the verdict is restricted to that setting. R1 remains outside the versions; the V5 verdict relies on explicitly identified missing results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label performance.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance; Muon is compared with AdamW using loss-to-target and compute-time measures.
Held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and large batches.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Sharpness or other measured properties related to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: 500M parameter models
rows.operation_detail: Compared tokens consumed by Muon and AdamW to reach the same target loss across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Tokens required to reach a target training loss; authors report Muon requires 10–15 % fewer tokens than AdamW to reach an identical loss.
rows.value: Muon requires 10–15 % fewer tokens than AdamW
rows.note: This is training-loss/data-efficiency evidence, not a measurement of held-out error or the training–test gap.
rows.check: The optimizer token-efficiency ratio does not itself measure the within-optimizer batch-size penalty named by V5. The 10–15% figure summarizes the conclusion across experiments; it is not established as a result specific to the stated 500M condition. Describe the loss as fresh-batch loss used as a generalization proxy, rather than dismissing it solely because it is called training loss.

relationships.condition: 500M Gemma 3 on DCLM, AdamW and Muon, batches above 3.5M tokens near loss 3.25
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Appendix D.1 reports increasing tokens needed for the same fresh-batch loss above 3.5M for both optimizers, implying a penalty at a fixed token budget; the increase is slower with Muon.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports that batches above the optimal size needed more tokens, with token requirements rising more slowly for Muon. This unverified comparison uses loss on a fresh batch as a proxy and suggests, rather than directly measures, a loss penalty under a fixed budget.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: 500M Gemma 3 on DCLM, AdamW and Muon, batches above 3.5M tokens near loss 3.25
source_check.reason: Appendix D.1 and Figure 10 identify 3.5M as token-optimal at loss 3.25 for both optimizers; token requirements increase beyond it, more slowly with Muon. This supports a fixed-token-budget penalty using the authors' fresh-batch generalization proxy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
